Written up as `claude/ROUND6_unscreened_sweep.md`. Your mid-turn idea turned out to produce the sharpest single result, so let me start there.

## Your slice idea found a hole in our own screen

Operations trivial on the slice, nontrivial off it — applied to machinery we already built and verified, this is concrete.

Round 3 recorded, without pursuing it: *"in the integrable-systems parametrisation the diagonal is the Calogero–Moser momentum, **left free**, and pinning it to $Y_{jj} = \sum_{k\neq j} 2/(z_j-z_k)$ is exactly the constraint that makes the $t_2$ flow the heat flow."* And round 4 established the pencil identity is **Wilson's tau function** $\tau(t) = \det(X + \sum_{i\geq1} i\,t_i Z^{i-1})$ restricted to $t_1 = z$, $t_2 = t$, everything else zero.

So the CM fibre over a given characteristic polynomial is a whole family projecting to the same polynomial, and $t_3, t_4, \dots$ — the higher KP flows — are **entirely unused directions**. They're nontrivial off the projection and trivial on it, exactly your construction.

**The hole:** Rodgers–Tao gives $\Lambda \geq 0$ in the **$t_2$ direction**. RH $\iff \Lambda = 0$ makes $\Xi$ a boundary point of the hyperbolic locus *in that direction*. Round 5's marginality screen then rejects any positivity mechanism holding "with room to spare" — but with room to spare *in $t_2$*. **A mechanism robust in a $t_3$ or $t_4$ direction is not refuted by Rodgers–Tao at all.** We applied the screen as though it covered all directions. It doesn't.

Open questions this generates, none of which we ever asked: do the higher KP flows preserve hyperbolicity? Is there a DBN-type constant per flow, and is $\Xi$ marginal or *interior* in those directions? Independent corroboration that the region is empty — the sweep's own void list records that nobody has connected the DBN heat flow to any gauge-theoretic or instanton flow, despite both being one-parameter families with a critical value at $t=0$. Our round-2 pencil result *is* that connection and it's still unwritten.

Also worth noting: your framing may open a second hole. Screen B rules out invariants that are locally constant on $\mathbb{C}^d \setminus \{\Delta = 0\}$. It says nothing about *relative* invariants of an extension problem — the obstruction to extending off-slice. That's a different cohomology and the screen doesn't reach it.

## The Males–Ono check: closed, negative — I was wrong

Two corrections. First, `arXiv:2204.05465` is **Johnston–Males**; Ono is not an author. Rounds 2 and 5 both had this wrong, and it mattered to my reasoning.

Second, the result is GORZ-shaped and silent on uniformity — Theorem 1.7 reads *"For fixed $r$ and $p$, as $n \to \infty$ … satisfy all order $k$ Turán inequalities,"* with no $N(k)$ and no discussion of $k$-dependence. And the stratification kills my hypothesis precisely: modularity produces the exact Rademacher formula, the Rademacher formula produces an asymptotic expansion, and **the hyperbolicity step consumes only that expansion.** Integrality plays no role. So round 2's dismissal was right and my objection to it was wrong.

## But the framing I gave you for the gap was wrong, and this matters more

I told you the gap is: error grows with $d$, Hermite's root gap shrinks with $d$. The numbers are right ($\min\text{-gap}(H_d) \approx 2.22\,d^{-1/2}$, spread $\approx \sqrt d$), but **that's a property of the GORZ method, not of the problem.** Kim–Lee (JKMS 2022) get $N(\Xi;d) = O(d^{1/2+\varepsilon})$ — sublinear polynomial, far better than the exponential I quoted — using Gauss–Lucas plus Obreschkoff, with **no Hermite comparison and no asymptotics at all.**

Here's the real structure, which appears to be unwritten anywhere:

> Every known result has the form "$J^{d,n}$ hyperbolic when $d \leq f(n)$." But $\Xi \in LP$ follows from hyperbolicity of $J^{d,0}$ for all $d$. **RH is the single vertical line $n=0$, $d\to\infty$ — the one direction every known wedge is empty in by construction.** Improving $f$ from $2\log n$ to $n^{2-\varepsilon}$ to $n^{100}$ doesn't move toward RH at all. **It's a change of quantifier order, not a quantitative deficit.**

And a sharp negative that constrains everything: for $p(n)$, the higher-order Turán inequality **fails** for $n < 95$ but holds for each fixed $d$ at large $n$. So the GORZ hypothesis is satisfied by a sequence where the uniform conclusion is *false* — **no method using only GORZ-type asymptotics can ever prove uniformity.** Any uniform mechanism must use something $\Xi$ has that $p(n)$ lacks.

Consequence for our own work: the margin map and the edge law measure the price of finite-$d$ certificates *along a direction that doesn't approach the target line*. They stand as measurements; "the critical path to RH" was the wrong label.

Two mechanisms do have the right shape. **Finite-verification-in / uniform-out**: verified RH to height $T$ gives hyperbolicity for *all* $n$ when $d \lesssim T^2$ (Kim–Lee Thm 4 gets $d \leq 9\times10^{24}$ for every $n$). And **a uniform root-separation mesh** — Iskander–Jain's $\delta$-Laguerre–Pólya class, uniform in $d$ *by construction* because the mesh is $d$-independent and $H_d$ never appears. Executed only for Bessel-type special functions, never for an arithmetic sequence.

Also: **nobody has uniformity for any natural sequence.** And it's provably unavoidable at Kim–Lee's generality — their hypothesis class contains RH-false functions, so $N(d)\to\infty$ is forced. Ki says it in one line: *"too general to control zeros of genuine zeta functions."*

## The kernel side turned our screen into a theorem — and killed my own idea

**Newman 1976 completely characterized** the kernels whose real-rootedness survives *any* Gaussian slack: decay no faster than Gaussian-quartic. $\Phi$ decays doubly exponentially. It misses by an entire regime.

That yields a rigorous no-go we only had as a heuristic:

> Any kernel criterion that (i) implies real-rootedness and (ii) is stable under $K \mapsto e^{-\varepsilon u^2}K$ for some $\varepsilon > 0$ **must fail for $\Phi$** — otherwise $\Lambda \leq -\varepsilon < 0$, contradicting Rodgers–Tao. **No robust kernel criterion can ever verify RH.**

And my total-positivity suggestion is **provably dead**: by Schoenberg, a PF$_\infty$ function's bilateral Laplace transform is $1/\psi$ with $\psi$ zero-free, but $\int\Phi e^{-su}du = 2\Xi(is)$ is entire with infinitely many zeros. $\Phi$ is log-concave (PF$_2$) but not PF$_\infty$, necessarily.

**One reversal of round 5.** $\Phi$ satisfies the full convexity tower — log-concave, $V'(t)/t$ increasing (Csordas–Varga 1988), $V'$ convex on $[0,\infty)$ (Newman 1991) — and that last one is exactly the GHS condition. So **RH isn't analogous to a Lee–Yang problem, it *is* one, exactly**: $\Phi\,du$ is a genuine GHS-class single-site spin measure, $\int e^{hs}\Phi(s)ds$ *is* $\Xi$, and "zeros on the imaginary $h$-axis" *is* RH. Simon–Griffiths locate the miss precisely: $\varphi^4$ is Lee–Yang, $\varphi^6$ isn't, Newman's class *is* $\varphi^4$, and $\Phi$ is super-quartic-confining. Round 5's gauge-content point stands, but "terminates at Lee–Yang" undersold it badly.

The one live kernel candidate: Csordas' positive-definiteness of the derived kernels $K_n(t;\Phi_\lambda)$ with a sign change at $\lambda = 0$ (Open Problem 4.10) — promising *because* it isn't obviously Gaussian-stable, so it escapes the no-go.

## Three more findings worth flagging

**Bombieri–Garrett is a quantitative no-go, not a slogan.** Eigenvalue spacings for any designed pseudo-Laplacian must exceed $\sim(1/2-\varepsilon)\pi/\log T$, while Montgomery predicts $\approx 11.3\%$ of consecutive zero pairs are closer. So **at most $\approx 94\%$ of $\zeta$'s zeros can appear in the spectrum of any *single* operator.** Sierra independently concedes *"one needs to fine tune a parameter to see each individual zero."* Two directions converging on: one operator per zero, not one for all. Nobody has asked whether a *family* — a spectral sheaf over the parameter — evades the ceiling.

**Jensen polynomials have never been applied to any gauge-theoretic counting sequence.** Not Nekrasov $Z_k$, not DT, PT, GV, or VW. Mature technology, available asymptotics, empty intersection. Nearest foothold is suggestive: Heim–Neuhauser *with Appendix B by Ken Ono* (arXiv:2606.15394) get a unique real negative simple dominant zero of the Nekrasov–Okounkov polynomials via **Perron–Frobenius on an explicit nonnegative Hessenberg matrix.** One real zero from mere nonnegativity. Concrete unasked question: **is that matrix totally nonnegative, and is $\{A_{n,k}\}$ a Pólya frequency sequence?** (This survives the $\Phi$ kill — the obstruction was about $\Phi$, not about a gauge sequence.)

**An unwalked chain, every link published, no paper spanning more than two:** Chern–Simons Stokes constants (integers, conjecturally DT) → resurgence → quantum modular forms → McSpirit–Rolen ($L$-function functional equations are the *computational input* to Stokes constants) → Bettin–Conrey (those period functions carry **Vasyunin sums**) → **Vasyunin sums are exactly the Nyman–Beurling criterion for RH.** Quantum modularity is the one place in the landscape where physics *produces* new arithmetic rather than consuming it — and the chain terminates at the RH criterion we've never used, which is far more hospitable to a physical construction than Pólya's.

Sweep is complete — written up as `claude/ROUND7_nonlinear_preservers_and_KP.md`. Leading with the bad news, since it's mine.

## The KP idea is dead, and I should have caught it myself

The question was genuinely unasked in the literature. The answer is elementary and I could have derived it before getting excited.

First a small positive: the pencil identity extends to **every** KP time, verified symbolically in exact arithmetic for $k=2,\dots,6$ —

$$\det(zI - X - s\,Z^{k-1}) = \exp\!\left(-\tfrac{s}{k}\partial_z^k\right)p_0(z)$$

So each higher flow acts on a rational-KP tau function as a *generalized* heat semigroup. Which reduces my question to "is $e^{tz^k}$ in the Laguerre–Pólya class" — because $\varphi(\partial_z)$ preserves hyperbolicity iff $\varphi \in \mathcal{LP}$ (Pólya–Schur / Hermite–Poulain, and the forward direction is just that $\varphi(\partial_z)z^n$ is a reversed Jensen polynomial). And **every Laguerre–Pólya function has order $\leq 2$**, from the normal form $e^{-\alpha z^2+\beta z+\gamma}z^m\prod(1-z/x_k)$. So $e^{tz^k}$ is out for every $k \geq 3$.

Checkable in one line: $\exp(t\partial^3)(z^3-z) = z^3 - z + 6t$, discriminant $4 - 972t^2$ — hyperbolic only for $|t| \leq 2/\sqrt{972}$, then never again. And $\exp(t\partial^4)z^4 = z^4 + 24t$ fails for both signs.

**So the hole in our screen is real and empty.** In a $t_k$ direction a hyperbolic polynomial is genuinely *interior* to a bounded interval, so marginality doesn't bite — but there's no positivity mechanism to be robust in, because the flow doesn't preserve hyperbolicity at all. The contrast is worth stating flatly: under $t_2$ the flow *acquires* hyperbolicity at a threshold and keeps it forever, which is what makes $\Lambda$ meaningful. Under $t_k$, $k\geq3$, it *loses* hyperbolicity and never recovers. **The higher KP flows are anti-de-Bruijn–Newman.** The $t_2$ direction isn't one option among many; Pólya–Schur says it's the only one.

## The real result: mesh, not real-rootedness

Two tracks converged without looking for each other.

**Uniformity in $d$** (round 6): the only route anyone has walked to $d$-uniform hyperbolicity is Iskander–Jain's **$\delta$-Laguerre–Pólya class** — defined by a $d$-independent lower bound $\delta$ on root *separation*. Uniform by construction, because $H_d$ never enters.

**The $q$-deformation** (this round): Brändén–Krasikov–Shapiro **prove** that no nontrivial finite-difference operator preserves all real-rooted polynomials, so they're forced to work with mesh $\geq \alpha$ instead. Lamprecht and Leake–Ryder then build the whole $q$-theory around **log-mesh**, and note explicitly that $q$-multiplicative convolution does *not* preserve real-rootedness — it preserves log-mesh.

> Root separation is the invariant that survives both obstructions. Two unrelated problems force the same substitution.

**But I want to flag the likely killer rather than bury it:** a mesh bound needs the zeros not to crowd, and Lehmer pairs are precisely zeta zeros that crowd. So $\Xi$ plausibly has no uniform mesh bound at all, which would make the $\delta$-LP route inapplicable for a structural reason. Cheap to check numerically against our existing zero caches, and worth doing before investing.

## On your $q$ question specifically

No $q$-analogue of Pólya's criterion exists, and there's a clean reason. The naive $q$-Jensen polynomial applied to $\gamma \equiv 1$ — the best possible input, since $e^z$ is the canonical LP function — gives **exactly the Rogers–Szegő polynomial**, and all its zeros lie on $|X| = 1$ (verified to 60 digits). Because $\binom{d}{j}_q = \binom{d}{d-j}_q$, the thing is self-inversive; the $q$-deformation rotates the zero locus from $\mathbb{R}$ to the unit circle. Rogers–Szegő is the $q$-analogue of the binomial and the one family in the $q$-Askey scheme orthogonal on the circle rather than the line — not a coincidence.

There is a repair, and it looks new: insert the Gauss weight $q^{\binom{j}{2}}$. For $\gamma\equiv1$ the $q$-binomial theorem then gives $\prod_{i=0}^{d-1}(1+q^iX)$ — hyperbolic, roots $-q^{-i}$ in geometric progression with log-mesh exactly $q$. Tested across LP and non-LP inputs it tracks LP membership correctly, including failing *only at small shift* for $(1+z^2)e^z$, which is the classical signature. And the weight is the exact inverse of Leake–Ryder's $q$-multiplicative convolution weight, so it lands inside the existing framework rather than nowhere. Open: no $q$-analogue of Borcea–Brändén exists — nobody has classified log-mesh-preserving operators.

## Four other things

**Our round-3 pencil question is confirmed unaddressed, and the answer inverts a background assumption.** No literature anywhere on "for which pencils is $\text{spec}(X+tY)$ real for all $t \geq t_0$" — the whole theory is pointwise. Worked out this round: eventual reality holds if $Y$ has *distinct* eigenvalues (27% failure without it), and **reality is genuinely not monotone in $t$** — of 400 random $4\times4$ instances, 83 gave two intervals and 8 gave three. So $\Lambda(p) = \inf\{t : \text{spec real}\}$ being a true one-sided threshold is *not* generic pencil behaviour. **Something about the rank-one CM condition forces monotonicity, and identifying what is a well-posed question we never asked.** That's the right form of round 3 §3.4.

**Round 5 disqualified MTV on the wrong grounds.** The Shapovalov positivity is used *purely qualitatively* — only to switch on the spectral theorem — and the norms are $z$-independent, so there's no degeneration. The genuinely tight inputs are (i) exact reality of the marked points, which the symmetry needs on the nose over a measure-zero closed set, and (ii) **eigenvalue simplicity**, which positivity doesn't supply and which is the fragile piece. Corroboration: Levinson–Purbhoo prove a generalization by a purely topological argument with no positive form anywhere. Another inherited screen applied to the wrong ingredient.

**Your projection idea shows up as a theorem in Harnack curves.** Simple Harnack ⟺ the amoeba map is at most 2-to-1 (the only collapsing is conjugation) ⟺ **maximal amoeba area** ⟺ the logarithmic Gauss map is *totally real*. Total reality is equivalent to an **extremality condition on the projection** — and that matters because it is *not* a positivity certificate, which is the only kind our marginality screen kills. (Also: KOS and KO were swapped in our notes; the closed-octant result is Kenyon–Okounkov, Duke 131.)

**And the quaternionic observation Stage 0 should have made.** For slice-regular $f$ with real coefficients, $V(f)$ is isolated real points plus isolated 2-spheres, one per conjugate pair. So $f$ is hyperbolic $\iff$ $V(f)$ contains **no 2-spheres** $\iff \dim V(f) = 0$ — real-rootedness as a *topological* condition in four dimensions, with the sphere radius $|y|$ equal to the imaginary part, so it's quantitative rather than yes/no. Stage 0 failed by trying to use the symmetry, which was free; the content is in the radii. And the apparatus exists: **Perotti's four-dimensional Jensen formula** (arXiv:1902.06485) plus Gentili–Vignozzi quaternionic Weierstrass products — Jensen's formula and canonical products being exactly the engine classical Laguerre–Pólya theory runs on. Nobody has run it here. (Fueter regularity is the wrong category — $q^n$ isn't Fueter regular for $n\geq2$, so it can't host a theory of polynomial roots at all.)

Clean negatives: no tropical Pólya/Jensen criterion; no dimer/Harnack ↔ zeta connection (high confidence, no citation overlap); no MTV → gauge-vacua translation; no credible quaternionic–RH work (the one MDPI *Symmetry* paper claiming to prove RH is fatally flawed and its quaternionic content is decorative).

Graeffe deserves a footnote for being *exactly* wrong for us: it separates moduli and destroys signed separation, and collides $\pm a$ pairs — and $\Xi$'s zero set is symmetric.

---

Six live items are listed at the end of the doc. The cheapest and most decisive is the mesh check on $\Xi$'s Jensen polynomials — if the mesh collapses, that closes the one route to $d$-uniformity anyone has found, and it runs on data we already have.

**Route 4 is closed, twice over — and by a computation I should have run in round 6 instead of proposing it.**

The Hessenberg question collapses to one question: by Aissen–Schoenberg–Whitney–Edrei, $\{A_{n,k}\}$ is a Pólya frequency sequence iff its generating polynomial — which *is* the Nekrasov–Okounkov polynomial — has only real nonpositive roots, and a totally nonnegative matrix forces the same. So: are the NO polynomials real-rooted? **No, from $n=10$**, exact Sturm counts on squarefree integer polynomials, first failure exhibitable:

$$P_{10}(u) = \tfrac{1}{3628800}\,u(u+1)\big(u^8 + 134u^7 + 6496u^6 + \cdots + 6531840\big)$$

with two complex pairs in the octic. So Heim–Neuhauser–Ono's Perron–Frobenius result isn't the first rung of a total-positivity ladder; it's the whole ladder.

But that was the wrong object anyway — parameter polynomials, not counting sequences. So I ran the screen route 4 actually wanted, on the Vafa–Witten/K3 sequence $a(n) = [q^n]\prod(1-q^k)^{-24}$. Two results:

- $N(d) = 0$ for all $d \le 8$ — hyperbolic at *every* shift, far better than $p(n)$ where $N(3) = 94$.
- And then $J^{13,0}$ **is not hyperbolic** — 9 real roots, two complex pairs at $-0.381 \pm 0.029i$ and $-0.269 \pm 0.017i$. Exact Sturm, confirmed independently.

So the VW generating function isn't in the Laguerre–Pólya class, and $\Xi$ is qualitatively different: margin ratio to Hermite at $d=8$ is 0.49 for $\Xi$ versus 0.081 for VW, and $\Xi$'s $J^{d,0}$ is verified hyperbolic to $d=80$ while VW dies at 13. **The hope was a transportable uniformity mechanism; the nearest gauge sequence doesn't have the property to transport.** What survives is a small publishable measurement — nobody has done Jensen polynomials for any gauge counting sequence, and this locates Johnston–Males's asymptotic theorem precisely, giving a second worked example after $p(n)$ of "each $d$, large $n$" holding while "all $d$, all $n$" fails.

**Route 5's chain is dead, but it decomposes and the surviving half is the best item in the brief.**

Four defects: McSpirit–Rolen runs $L\text{-function} \to \text{Stokes data}$, which is **backwards** for producing RH; it concerns Zagier's examples, not Chern–Simons objects; Bettin–Conrey's carriers are "imperfect" quantum modular forms differing by a non-smooth correction; and Stokes integrality is conjectural, verified for $4_1$ and $5_2$ only. One conjectural link, two species mismatches, one reversed arrow.

What survives is independent of the chain. First, quantum modularity really is the one place physics *produces* arithmetic — the object was invented because Chern–Simons asymptotics demanded it, whereas every other physics/RH contact in rounds 1–7 consumes known arithmetic. Second, and this is the actionable part: **retarget from Pólya to Nyman–Beurling.** It's a density statement in a Hilbert space rather than a hyperbolicity statement about polynomials; it has no $d$, so round 6's quantifier-order problem doesn't arise; it's exactly critical, so the Gaussian-slack no-go doesn't apply; its Gram matrices are Vasyunin cotangent sums, which is the closest thing in the whole survey to an integral structure with a definiteness question; and it has the same shape as Connes' current route — finite truncations behave, the limit is the difficulty. Counterweight recorded honestly: it's a known equivalence with decades of effort behind it, so switching criteria isn't progress by itself. The question that would make it progress is whether anything physical supplies the density statement.

**Route 3 isn't closed, and the reason to keep it is narrow but real.** It's tautological in the certificate sense — for real-coefficient $f$ the quaternionic zero set is *determined* by the slice data, sphere radii being $|\text{Im}\,\rho|$, which is Stage 0's failure recurring. But re-deriving the screens rather than inheriting them: "$V(f)$ contains no 2-spheres" is *exactly equivalent* to hyperbolicity, so it has no slack to be Gaussian-stable in. Round 6 §3 concluded only exactly-critical criteria can possibly work. **This one is exactly critical, and almost nothing else is.**

Everything then turns on one checkable question: does Perotti's four-dimensional Jensen formula, specialized to real coefficients, reduce to classical Jensen or carry extra terms? I predict it reduces — a 3-sphere at a real point fibres over the 2-sphere of imaginary units with circle fibres, and $f|_{L_I}$ is the same function for every $I$. But the formula uses the value *and first two derivatives*, which is more data than classical Jensen, so my prediction may be wrong. One afternoon, binary outcome.

---

Ranking for the next thread: route 5(b) first (cheap, it's a reframing), then route 3's deciding check, then the McSpirit–Rolen arrow direction, with route 4 closed. The five scripts are in the workspace if you want to rerun or extend — say the word and I'll send them.

And one methodological note I put in the doc because it bit again: round 6 §10 said re-derive inherited screens before applying them.
